author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Verify logs and screenshots after changing the emulator data folder
summary: After relocating emulator data, create one uniquely named screenshot and one marked log session, confirm both land only in the new paths, survive app restart, and remain writable before deleting or archiving the old folder.
heroAlt: PCSX2 screenshot directory containing clearly grouped game captures for path verification

sourceLabels.android-storage: Android file access and storage concepts

blocks.text: Create unmistakable artifacts in the new location

A migrated data folder can appear correct while screenshots still go to an old directory or logs silently fail because Android permission is read-only. Before removing anything, create artifacts whose names and timestamps cannot be confused with earlier files. Use a visible in-game marker for the screenshot and a short log session containing a known launch event.
Do not delete the old data directory until configuration, saves, screenshots, and logs have been verified after a full app restart. Keep a recoverable backup outside both paths.
Record both old and new paths

items: Old data folder copied to a separate backup location.
New folder authorized with persistent read and write access.
Exact old and new screenshot, log, save, and cache subpaths documented.
A title that launches from a normal save without modifying critical progress.
A timestamp or marker phrase for the verification session.

blocks.text: Write, locate, restart, and write again

items: 1. Open the configured data path and note the current time before launch.
2. Start the test title and trigger one screenshot at a unique visible frame.
3. Enable the normal diagnostic log and create a known launch or settings event.
4. Close the emulator cleanly and inspect both new output files.
5. Confirm neither artifact was written only to the old directory.
6. Reopen the app, verify the data path remains selected, and create a second screenshot.
7. Read the log tail and open both images to prove they are valid, not zero-byte placeholders.
8. Archive the old folder only after saves and configuration also pass their own checks.

blocks.text: A two-launch test verifies both immediate write access and persisted path selection. Unique visual and log markers prevent old files from being mistaken for success. Opening the outputs catches placeholder files created before a permission or storage failure.
The migration passes when fresh artifacts are valid, correctly placed, and repeat after process restart.

items: Screenshot and log timestamps match the test session.
Both files open and contain the expected marker.
The old directory receives no unintended new output.
The selected path persists through a full app restart.
The backup remains untouched until all data classes pass.
Files appear only until restart: renew persistent folder authorization.
Logs update but screenshots do not: inspect their separate configured subpaths.
Zero-byte output appears: stop and check free space and write permission.
Two identical folders are confused: compare resolved paths and timestamps.

blocks.text: Return to the old path if any artifact fails

Select the original verified data folder, restart the emulator, and confirm one screenshot and log session there. Preserve the failed new folder for inspection, but do not merge newer files blindly over the backup.
Android providers can expose virtual paths

A document provider may display a friendly name that is not a traditional filesystem path, and permissions can be provider-specific. Validate behavior through actual writes and restart persistence rather than relying only on the folder label. Confirm that a newly created screenshot and log have current timestamps, nonzero sizes, and can be reopened through Android after the emulator is closed. Keep the old output folder until the new destination passes two launches, because a visible directory alone does not prove durable write access.
